errors.claim: Sustainability reporting is a now-mainstream extension of corporate accountability.
errors.source_check: The source reports adoption by 93% of the world's 250 largest companies, but also says sustainability reporting is still relatively new and not yet mandatory.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier that reporting is widely adopted among the world's largest companies while still relatively new and non-mandatory

errors.claim: Merchandising firms' cost of goods sold is derived from purchase cost plus mark-up.
searches: what it cost them to acquire|difference.*paid.*revenue
errors.source_check: The source defines cost of goods sold as what the merchant paid to acquire the goods. The mark-up is added to acquisition cost to establish the selling price; it is not part of cost of goods sold.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to cost of goods sold is the acquisition cost, while purchase cost plus mark-up determines selling price

errors.claim: Service organisations "earn revenue by providing intangible products".
searches: earn revenue by providing intangible products|intangible products
errors.source_check: The source says, "A service organization is a business that earns revenue by providing intangible products." The quoted fragment changes "earns" to "earn".
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "earns revenue by providing intangible products" or remove quotation marks and paraphrase

errors.claim: The contribution margin income statement is "a specialized income statement [...] used to determine how changes in sales volume impact the bottom line".
searches: to determine how changes in sales volume impact|used to determine how changes
errors.source_check: The source says, "we can create a specialized income statement called a contribution margin income statement to determine how changes in sales volume impact the bottom line." It does not contain the quoted wording "used to determine".
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "a specialized income statement called a contribution margin income statement" used "to determine how changes in sales volume impact the bottom line"

errors.claim: A production cost report is "the report that shows the costs used in the preparation of a product...".
searches: shows the costs used in the preparation|the report that shows
errors.source_check: The body says, "This report shows the costs used..." and the glossary says, "production cost report shows the costs used..." The quoted phrase "the report that shows" is absent.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "shows the costs used in the preparation of a product..." or paraphrase without quotation marks

errors.claim: Absorption-costing decisions led the Big Three auto companies to manufacture more vehicles than demand because allocating fixed overhead to inventory lowered apparent unit cost.
searches: Big Three auto|more vehicles than the market demanded
not the only reason|manufacturing too many cars|period costs hidden
errors.source_check: The source makes this connection but explicitly qualifies it: "While this was not the only reason for manufacturing too many cars, it kept the period costs hidden among the manufacturing costs."
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier that absorption costing was not the only reason for overproduction

errors.claim: Most companies move from centralised toward decentralised structures as they grow.
errors.source_check: The source says decentralisation is an alternative for growing businesses and that a company will "often decentralize" as it grows; it does not quantify this as "most companies".
errors.suggested_fix: correct to companies often move toward decentralisation as they grow

errors.claim: For each of the five responsibility-centre types, the text develops a worked example using Apparel World.
searches: discretionary cost center|Southwest Airlines|Best Buy|five types
errors.source_check: Apparel World supplies the worked cost-centre and profit-centre reports and later ROI/RI calculations. The revenue-centre example is Southwest Airlines, the investment-centre definition cites Best Buy or the food trucks, and no equivalent Apparel World worked example is developed for every type.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to Apparel World supplies worked cost-centre and profit-centre examples and later investment-performance calculations, not an example for every centre type

errors.claim: A segment earning 25.9% ROI may reject a project earning 18%, while residual income would favour it.
errors.source_check: The reference splices two examples. In Chapter 9 the segment earns 25.9%, while the proposed $50,000 play-area project earns $5,001 (just over 10%). The 18% project appears in Chapter 12, where the division's existing ROI is 20%.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to either 25.9% current ROI versus just over 10% for the play-area project, or 20% current ROI versus an 18% project

errors.claim: The volume recommends the contribution-margin approach as the primary tool for keep-or-discontinue decisions.
searches: Two basic approaches|compare contribution margins and fixed costs
errors.source_check: The source presents contribution-margin and net-income analysis as two basic approaches and says the net-income approach requires more information. It does not designate or recommend contribution margin as the primary tool.
errors.suggested_fix: delete the claim that the volume recommends it as the primary tool

errors.claim: The chapter closes by saying sustainability reporting "moves us a long way from merely reporting the financial results of businesses [...] and helps bind us all...".
searches: Social responsibility reporting has moved us a long way
It provides a foundation|helps bind us all
errors.source_check: The source says, "Social responsibility reporting has moved us a long way from merely reporting the financial results of businesses." A separate following sentence contains "it helps bind us all" after an intervening foundation clause. The reference changes the subject and tense and splices the sentences.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to the source's exact two sentences or paraphrase without quotation marks

errors.claim: Patagonia's annual giving commitment is 1% of sales or 10% of pre-tax profits.
searches: Patagonia has donated|1% of its annual sales
10% of its pre-tax profits|whichever is greater
errors.source_check: The source says Patagonia donated 1% of annual sales or 10% of pre-tax profits, "whichever is greater."

errors.claim: Approximately 5,000 mechanics work at Fiat Chrysler's Belvidere Assembly Plant.
errors.source_check: The source says there are approximately 5,000 "employees assembling automobiles" at the plant. It does not identify them as mechanics.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to approximately 5,000 employees assembling automobiles

errors.claim: The source implicitly attributes just-in-time manufacturing and lean practices to the Toyota Production System and Taiichi Ohno.
errors.source_check: Taiichi Ohno and the name "Toyota Production System" are absent. The source says lean practices were implemented by Toyota Motor Corporation soon after World War II and that JIT was initiated by Toyota Motor Corporation.
errors.suggested_fix: delete Taiichi Ohno and Toyota Production System; attribute the practices only to Toyota Motor Corporation

errors.claim: For more than 30 years, Patagonia donated 1% of annual sales or 10% of pre-tax profits.
searches: 1% of its annual sales|10% of its pre-tax profits
errors.source_check: The source includes the essential qualifier "whichever is greater" after the two percentages.

errors.claim: The source implicitly references the Cox-Blake business case on diversity benefits in Chapter 1.5.
errors.source_check: Cox-Blake is absent, and Chapter 1.5 does not present the claimed diversity-benefits connection.

errors.claim: In the SnowBucks example, the contribution-margin approach is recommended.
searches: Two basic approaches|contribution margin approach|net income approach
errors.source_check: The source uses relevant-cost and contribution-margin analysis to show that allocated common costs created a misleading loss, but it presents two basic analytical approaches and does not expressly recommend contribution margin over net income.
errors.suggested_fix: delete "the contribution-margin approach is recommended" and state that relevant-cost analysis reveals the misleading common-cost allocation
